title: Quack process environment
description: The variables quack's processes read. The root is the deployment environment the operator sets on the distributor; the extension apps mount in that same process, so their reads are root properties, required exactly when the deployment file lists them. $defs/session is the environment the session runtime receives, assembled by the driver at launch. The rule for the root: it holds secrets, and a narrow, named set of process variables — the deployment's own paths, its listener ports, and build metadata. Nothing else. Secrets are the provider and keyed-service API keys (named by the deployment file's providers.*.apiKeyEnv and services.*.apiKeyEnv), the postgres store URLs (stores.*.urlEnv), and the named secrets of this schema, each declared by the reader's manifest. Process variables are QUACK_DATA_DIR, QUACK_CONFIG, QUACK_AGENTS_DIR, QUACK_WEB_DIR, PORT, QUACK_SESSION_PORT, QUACK_COMMIT and QUACK_BUILT_AT. A deployment setting that is neither is a defect here: it belongs in the deployment file (contracts:608df0111). Absent by design, with their new home in one target revision — deployment.json v9, the next revision of contracts:608df0111, which gains exactly defaultAgent with defaultModel, the services map (exa, langfuse), the notifications section, the session driver section, and the github and remarkable settings: QUACK_EXA_URL and LANGFUSE_BASE_URL (the `services` map of keyed outbound services — Exa and Langfuse are entries, served by the outbound key proxy, contracts:5be69037), QUACK_VAPID_SUBJECT (the notifications section), QUACK_GH_AGENT, QUACK_GH_LABEL and QUACK_GH_APP_ID (extensions.github.settings), QUACK_REMARKABLE_AGENT, RMFAKECLOUD_URL and RMFAKECLOUD_EMAIL (extensions.remarkable.settings), the default agent QUACK_AGENT (with defaultModel), and QUACK_SESSION_DRIVER, QUACK_SESSION_IMAGE, QUACK_SESSION_RUNTIME, QUACK_SESSION_NETWORK, QUACK_ALLOW_RUNC, QUACK_SESSION_DISTRIBUTOR_URL, QUACK_DATA_VOLUME and QUACK_HOST_DATA_DIR (the session driver section, where the rule that exactly one data mount is set is expressed in the schema). QUACK_SESSION_PASSTHROUGH has no home: it is removed, and a session's secrets are declared by name in its agent's definition and delivered as 0600 files. The distributor refuses to start, naming the variable and where it moved, when any of these is set: the root is open, so a removed variable left set would otherwise be silently ignored — the worst failure for an operator. Required-or-not: QUACK_DATA_DIR and QUACK_CONFIG always; an app's or a service's secrets exactly when the deployment file lists the app or service; everything else optional with its failure stated per property; an incomplete credential pair fails at start, naming what is missing. Any name not listed here is allowed only as a secret the deployment file or an extension manifest claims (a provider or service key, or a store URL); validate checks the claim and names an unclaimed name. Every value is a string; a variable that parses to a number or boolean does so at its reader, and the failure of a non-numeric value is stated per property.

QUACK_DATA_DIR.description: The deployment's data directory: sessions' directories and agent versions, sqlite stores, and the generated VAPID keys all live under it. Read by the distributor at start, by every mounted app for its database file, and by the push module. Path. Required, no default. Not secret. Delivery: env. Missing or empty: the distributor throws 'QUACK_DATA_DIR is required' at start and never listens.

QUACK_CONFIG.description: The path of the deployment file (quack/deployment, contracts:608df0111): the deployment's providers, defaultModel, stores and extensions. Read by the distributor at start, and rewritten per session by the docker driver, which points the session at its own proxied copy. Path to a JSON file. Required, no default. Not secret — it names secrets, never holds them. Missing: 'QUACK_CONFIG is required'; unreadable or not JSON: 'reading <path>: <error>' — both before the first listener.

QUACK_AGENTS_DIR.description: The directory of agent definitions (<dir>/<agent>/agent.json>) the distributor lists as selectable agents and the schedules app scans for schedules registered by agents. Path. Optional. Not secret. Absent: no agents are listed and no schedules register; the distributor runs a data-dir-only install without error.

QUACK_WEB_DIR.description: The directory of the built web app the distributor serves. Path. Optional; the image sets it to /app/web. Not secret. Absent: a web asset request answers 404; no error.

QUACK_GH_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE.description: The path of the file holding the GitHub App's private key (PEM), read by the github app at mount. The long-form secret is delivered as a file: the environment carries the path, never the key. Path to a 0600 file. Required exactly when the deployment file lists extensions.github. Missing or unreadable while listed: the mount throws by name and the distributor exits.

QUACK_GH_WEBHOOK_SECRET.description: The shared value against which the github app verifies GitHub's webhook signatures. Secret. Required exactly when the deployment file lists extensions.github. Missing while listed: the mount throws 'QUACK_GH_WEBHOOK_SECRET is required by the github app' and the distributor exits.

QUACK_ADMIN_TOKEN.description: The bearer token for the operator-only session routes (rename, archive, delete) and the token the schedules retention sweep presents to delete idle sessions. Secret. Optional, no default. Absent: those routes answer 401 to a caller with no token and the sweep cannot delete — the features are off, silently.

QUACK_PROXY_SECRET.description: The shared value the reverse proxy sends in the x-quack-proxy-secret header to prove the identity header it forwards. Secret. Optional, no default. Absent: no identity header is ever believed and every request is a plain tailnet call — the safe default is deny. A wrong value behaves exactly like an absent one.

RMFAKECLOUD_PASSWORD.description: The rmfakecloud login's password — the secret of the login, read by the remarkable app at mount and never written in the deployment file. The login's address and email are not environment variables: they belong to the deployment file's extensions.remarkable.settings (deployment.json v9). Required exactly when the deployment file lists extensions.remarkable. Missing while listed: the mount throws 'RMFAKECLOUD_PASSWORD is required by the remarkable app' and the distributor exits.

LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY.description: The Langfuse project's public key. With its base URL and secret key it registers the LANGFUSE outbound route the traces extension posts to: the base URL is the deployment file's services.langfuse.baseUrl (deployment.json v9), and this key and its secret pair are named by the same services entry. Not a secret, but in a session container its value is replaced by the placeholder 'session' and the real key stays server-side with its pair. The key is required exactly when the deployment file lists services.langfuse; a listed entry with a key variable unset fails the distributor at start, naming the variable.

LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY.description: The Langfuse project's secret key — the secret of the pair, registered by the distributor as the LANGFUSE outbound route and delivered to a session container as its launch credential. Named by the deployment file's services.langfuse entry, whose baseUrl is the project's address. Required exactly when the deployment file lists services.langfuse; a listed entry with this variable unset fails the distributor at start, naming it — there is no silent no-route.

QUACK_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY.description: The web-push VAPID public key; with its private pair it overrides the keys generated once into <QUACK_DATA_DIR>/vapid.json (mode 0600) at first boot. The public half. Exactly one of the pair set: the distributor fails at start, naming the missing key — there is no silent ignore. Neither set: the generated file's keys are used.

QUACK_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY.description: The web-push VAPID private key — the secret of the pair, overriding the keys generated into <QUACK_DATA_DIR>/vapid.json. Exactly one of the pair set: the distributor fails at start, naming the missing key. Neither set: the generated file's keys are used. The push contact (subject) is not an environment variable: it belongs to the deployment file's notifications section.

PORT.description: The distributor's public listener: the reverse proxy and the tailnet. Port. Optional, default 8080. Not secret. Non-numeric: the bind fails at start with a Node socket error.

QUACK_SESSION_PORT.description: The port of the listener sessions dial; the public PORT never answers a session. Port. Optional, default PORT plus 1. Not secret. Non-numeric: the bind fails at start with a Node socket error.

QUACK_COMMIT.description: The image's commit, set by the image build from its build arg and served at /version. Build metadata. Optional; absent, /version answers null. Set by the image, not the operator. Not secret.

QUACK_BUILT_AT.description: When the image was built, set by the image build from its build arg and served at /version. Build metadata. Optional; absent, /version answers null. Set by the image, not the operator. Not secret.

^QUACK_[A-Z0-9_]+_API_KEY$.description: A provider's or a keyed service's API key, in the variable its id or its deployment file entry names (the id, non-alphanumerics upper-cased to underscores, between QUACK_ and _API_KEY, unless providers.*.apiKeyEnv or services.*.apiKeyEnv names another). Secret. Optional per provider and per service: a provider with no key runs keyless, as a local model server does; a service the deployment file lists without its key set fails the distributor at start, naming the variable. The distributor reads the value server-side and registers the entry's outbound proxy route through the generic keyed-service mechanism — nothing service-specific in core or in this contract; a session container's copy of the variable carries its launch credential instead, with the deployment file's entry re-routed to the proxy.

session.title: The session runtime's environment
session.description: What the session runtime process receives, assembled by the driver at launch; the operator never sets any of it. Beyond the named properties, the session carries the provider key variables of the deployment file, the variables the agent's extensions declare in their manifests, and the deployment extensions' variables (the traces trio). No host variable crosses undeclared: a secret the session genuinely needs is declared by name in its agent's definition and delivered by the driver as a 0600 file, read at boot and removed on read, like the launch credential. A process session's provider key variables hold the real keys; a container's hold its launch credential, and its deployment file is rewritten so every provider points at the outbound proxy. The launch variables (QUACK_SESSION_LISTENER_URL, QUACK_LAUNCH_TOKEN_FILE, QUACK_SESSION_TOKEN_FILE) are read by core at boot: the base URL from the environment, each credential from its 0600 file, removed on read; the runtime then primes the single SDK accessor in @quack/sdk and deletes the remaining launch names from its process environment, so a tool shell inherits none of them and no extension ever reads a launch variable itself — it gets the base URL and the outbound credential from the accessor, and the session server's bearer token never leaves core. A shell starts from the fixed toolchain allowlist (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, TZ, LANG, LANGUAGE, GOPATH, GOMODCACHE, GOCACHE, GOFLAGS, CARGO_HOME, RUSTUP_HOME, NVM_DIR), LC_*, and the names the deployment file's exec.env lists. A per-command shell variable — QUACK_GITHUB_URL, QUACK_GITHUB_TOKEN, QUACK_GH_REMOTE, set for one git invocation — is neither here nor in the deployment environment.

QUACK_CONFIG.description: The path of the deployment file the session's models and extensions are built from. In a container the driver re-points it at the session's own rewritten copy, /session/deployment.json, with every provider re-routed. Path. Always set by the driver. Unreadable or not JSON: the session fails at start, naming the path.

QUACK_AGENT.description: The agent definition the session runs, pinned at launch; in a container the driver rewrites the host path to the container mount. Path to an agent.json. Present for every session that runs: the runtime throws 'QUACK_AGENT is required' at start when it is absent, and the driver omits it only for a launch that resolved no agent, which then fails its first start.

QUACK_SESSION_DIR.description: The session's data directory: its open-session state and logs, and in a container the mounted subpath of the data volume. Path. Always set by the driver. Absent: the runtime throws 'QUACK_SESSION_DIR is required' at start.

QUACK_SESSION_KEY.description: The session's key, recorded on its index rows. The session key string. Required exactly when the session publishes — that is, exactly when QUACK_SESSION_LISTENER_URL and QUACK_LAUNCH_TOKEN_FILE are set; the driver sets all three together.

QUACK_SESSION_TOKEN_FILE.description: The path of the file holding the session server's bearer token: it authenticates distributor-to-session requests, which carry the decider's principal, so it effectively carries approval power, and it never leaves core — no accessor exposes it. The token is never an environment value: the environment stays readable, in /proc/<pid>/environ, to the session's own tool shells, while the file is written 0600 before launch, read at boot, and removed on read. Path. Always set by the driver. Missing, or empty on read: the runtime throws at start, before a resumed run can start a shell.

PORT.description: The port the session server binds. The process driver sets 0: the session picks a free port and reports it over IPC, so the parent never probes a port another process may take first. The docker driver sets 8080 inside the container. Port. Always set by the driver.

QUACK_SESSION_HOST.description: The interface the session server binds: 127.0.0.1 for a process session, 0.0.0.0 for a container, whose only path in is the distributor. Address. Always set by the driver.

QUACK_SESSION_LISTENER_URL.description: The base URL of the distributor's credentialed session listener: where the session publishes its index, how the lifecycle channel (contracts:233d9ccf) and its app calls reach the distributor. For a process session, loopback on the session port; for a container, the deployment file's session-section distributorUrl. Set by the driver as a pair with QUACK_LAUNCH_TOKEN_FILE; both absent and the session runs without a publisher and no outbound credential, silently. Read by core at boot; extensions get it from the SDK accessor, never the environment. Not secret itself — the credential is separate.

QUACK_LAUNCH_TOKEN_FILE.description: The path of the file holding this launch's outbound credential: the broker mints it per launch, the session presents it outbound (publishing, the lifecycle channel, app calls), and the broker revokes it when the session exits. It stays separate from the session server's bearer token (QUACK_SESSION_TOKEN_FILE), which points the other way — merging them would let anything holding the outbound credential call the session server as the distributor. The credential is never an environment value: the file is written 0600 before launch, read at boot, and removed on read; extensions get it from the SDK accessor. Secret. Set by the driver as a pair with QUACK_SESSION_LISTENER_URL; both absent and the session runs without a publisher, silently.
